headline: High: Plandex can write/egress by default while the paired awesome-list has no runtime isolation, creating leakage and conflict risks; prompt-injection is lower because the first agent is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot actively ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so manual copy-paste or file handoff could still carry malicious instructions into B, but the bridge is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B's stdin/stdout or project files, B may follow injected instructions.
IF B is configured to parse file contents as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted text from A into B.
Use a plain-text review step before feeding content to B.
Disable any auto-apply or auto-execute mode in B.
Keep A as a reference-only artifact, not an input source.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads/writes the filesystem and has broad network egress plus model-provider API calls. If A and B share a workspace, B can exfiltrate files from that workspace even though A itself is inert. The pairwise leakage path is therefore plausible in default B configurations.
conditions: IF A and B are placed in the same project directory, B can read shared files.
IF sensitive files are present in B's workspace, B can transmit them over network egress or to a model provider.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories.
Remove secrets from B's workspace before running.
Restrict B network access during review runs.
Use a redacted copy of any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write surface, but B can write the filesystem and modify git state. If both are pointed at the same repo or directory, B’s default write and git actions can overwrite or race with operator-managed artifacts. Uncertainty is low because A cannot coordinate or lock anything, so the conflict is driven by B’s mutable defaults.
conditions: IF A and B share the same git working tree, B can modify files that A is treating as reference material.
IF multiple B instances run against the same backend state, concurrent edits can conflict.
mitigations: Run B in a separate clone or branch.
Pause other B instances during edits.
Review git diffs before apply.
Keep A outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated reference list, not an executing agent, but B’s review-then-apply workflow can still treat external text as guidance. If A-derived recommendations are copied into B without verification, B may propagate mistakes into code changes or plans. The cascade exists, but A is not authoritative by default and B has a review step.
conditions: IF A-derived advice is pasted into B as task input, B may act on it without independent verification.
IF B is switched to auto-apply mode, erroneous upstream guidance can reach applied changes faster.
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived claims before use.
Keep B in review-then-apply mode.
Cross-check any A-sourced recommendation against primary docs.
Annotate copied text with source labels.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before apply.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source reference list with no touched data classes, while B handles source code and model-provider API keys. There is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch evidenced here, but B’s secret handling and networked model calls create a small compliance surface if operators place regulated data in its workspace. A is not cited for data residency because it has no such surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B's project directory, it may flow to external model providers.
IF the operator uses B on data subject to stricter retention rules, logs and API calls may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Review B's retention and logging settings.
Use a local-only model backend where possible.
Redact secrets before planning.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
